verdict.rationale: Cline uses external tools through MCP servers, and users can manage which MCP servers and plugins are installed. Auto Approve, with human-in-the-loop approval, sets which actions (including MCP tools) run without a prompt, so users keep tight control over high-risk actions. However, the evidence shows approval gating and user-level server management rather than an explicit access policy. Missing for 10: per-tool allow/deny lists for integrations, team- or org-level policy that an engineering lead can enforce, detailed docs on restricting MCP tool access, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: manage models, plugins, and MCP servers
MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Cline use external tools and data sources through MCP servers.

Auto Approve lets you decide which actions Cline can take without prompting you each time. It keeps you out of approval popups during routine work while letting you keep tight control over high-risk actions.
Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
